submission.justification: Crystal-K1 is excluded because its intrinsic background (2 counts/kg/day over 100-3000 keV) exceeds the hard budget of 0.5 counts/kg/day. Of the two survivors, K2 (0.3 counts/kg/day) and K3 (0.1 counts/kg/day) both pass the background limit. K2 gives the better energy resolution at 662 keV at every thickness tested: its best is 4.422% FWHM at 4 cm, versus 8.752% at 4 cm for K3 (K3's best across 2-10 cm is also 8.752% at 4 cm). Within K2, the scan over 2-10 cm (5.355, 4.939, 4.422, 4.731, 4.506, 5.421, 6.299 %) has its minimum at 4 cm. The 6 cm value (4.506%) is close, but 4 cm is the best. K2 at 4 cm therefore meets the goal of best achievable resolution and keeps background within budget with a 0.2 counts/kg/day margin. Caveat: the background figure is recorded as a single value per crystal, and no thickness dependence was reported, so I have assumed 0.3 counts/kg/day applies at 4 cm. K3 is the low-background alternative if background margin becomes more important than resolution.

Recommended thickness is 4 cm, within the 2-10 cm range.

requirements.requirement: Goal: best possible energy resolution at 662 keV
requirements.evidence: K2 at 4 cm gives 4.422% FWHM, the lowest resolution among the surviving candidates and tested thicknesses. K3 best is 8.752% (4 cm) and K2 at 6 cm is 4.506%, the next-best value.

requirements.evidence: Submitted Crystal-K2 at 4 cm via submit_recommendation.
